A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and three-page appendices. Reordered sections and renumbered supplementary displays can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original reconstruction, skeletonization, and segmentation experiments on synthetic Chenopodium plants and real scans, plus latent-dimension and latent-space analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds neuron-deactivation ablations and evaluation on virtual plants with greater structural complexity.

M1.justification: The recursive auto-encoders, classifiers, losses, PointNet mapping, and test-time optimization remain unchanged. Revised classifier wording and newly specified PointNet implementation details do not establish a changed algorithm.

E1.justification: v3 Section 10.7 adds evaluation on virtual Chenopodium plants at growth stages with structural complexity beyond training. The existing species, phenotyping tasks, clean/noisy/depth inputs, and five real scans are retained.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain SIREN; Livny, Xu, and Chaudhury's skeleton refinement; and PlantNet and PSegNet. Table 3 replaces citation numbers with comparator names without changing membership.

E3.justification: New protocols deactivate 75% of neurons separately in the node classifier, split classifier, and recursive encoder-decoder components, and evaluate tree-edit distance across plant complexity. Existing splits and benchmark metrics remain unchanged; newly disclosed training settings do not establish revised experiments.

E4.justification: v3 substantially broadens diagnostic evidence with component-wise neuron-deactivation ablations (Section 10.4, Table 5) and structural extrapolation tests (Section 10.7, Figure 12). v2's latent-dimension sensitivity, UMAP analysis, and noise/partial-input evaluations are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The new random neuron-deactivation experiment supplies no replication or uncertainty estimates.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports TED 0.196 for the full model versus 0.207, 0.204, and 0.240 for the three ablations. Figure 12 adds increasing TED with plant size, including unseen complexities. Tables 2–4 and the retained latent-dimension results are numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: The axial-tree representation, loss equations, and tree-edit-distance definition retain their mathematical substance. Decoder-symbol correction and explanatory rewording add no new assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: The multitask reconstruction and synthetic-to-real contribution claims remain. However, v3's conclusion qualifies the broad applicability claim by explicitly excluding monocotyledons such as wheat and maize because of plant-part observability requirements.

C2.justification: v3 explicitly discusses species-specific retraining, procedural training-data generation, manual node definitions, and the observability limitation. Section 10.7 newly interprets its complexity experiment as evidence of generalization, although Figure 12 shows increasing reconstruction error.

D1.justification: v3 adds code-repository and dataset-DOI access pointers. Section 9 newly specifies batch size 32, omission of PointNet's optional feature transformation, reduced layer dimensions, and an unscheduled point-encoder learning rate. These are additional disclosures rather than demonstrated implementation changes.

R1.justification: v3 adds Prusinkiewicz's 1986 Graphical Applications of L-Systems citation for geometric interpretation. The positioning relative to Demeter and task-specific approaches remains essentially unchanged; other bibliography edits mostly concern formatting and metadata.

P1.justification: Dataset moves before Method, and split/test descriptions move into Evaluation. v3 also makes localized prose corrections, revises the author block, and labels the appendix Supplementary Material. Most existing narrative remains intact.

P2.justification: v3 redraws Figure 4, names comparators directly in Table 3, and adds an ablation table and complexity plot. Existing skeleton and UMAP figures are relocated and renumbered, with local resizing and page reflow rather than a wholesale visual redesign.

improvement.justification: v3 improves assessability through component ablations, additional implementation and access information, and explicit applicability limits. These are useful incremental gains over v2. The complexity study lacks sample-count and uncertainty reporting, and its rising TED limits support for the optimistic generalization interpretation. The core method and benchmark evidence remain unchanged.
